summary: [Network Seminar] [Hybrid] - ECE/RBCCPS/CNI -- January 21, 2026 --    Aging Brain Research: Challenges and Opportunities
description:
Dear All,

Networks Seminar, supported by the Centre for Networked Intelligence, is a technical discussion forum in topics including but not limited to computer networks, machine learning, signal processing, and information theory. The seminar series has a webpage hosted at https://cni.iisc.ac.in/seminars/.

You are invited to the following seminar held as part of this series.

Title: Aging Brain Research: Challenges and Opportunities

Speaker: Professor K V S Hari, Director, Centre for Brain Research, Indian Institute of Science

Time: 4:00 PM - 5:00 PM (IST)

Date: 21 January 2026

Venue: GJ Hall and Online on Zoom

Zoom link: https://us06web.zoom.us/j/83388976389?pwd=XcpO3GhLxsR14a7SVbPx33HQQa1jbt.1

Zoom Meeting ID: 833 8897 6389, Pass Code: NSSIISc

YouTube Livestream: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F-qQcsGQhBg

Webpage Link: https://cni.iisc.ac.in/seminars/2026-01-21/

Abstract: Aging Brain research involves understanding the mechanisms of healthy and diseased aging in order to design appropriate interventions. The talk will present the issues related to cognitive decline and the current understanding about dementia. The challenges involved in assessing the status of cognitive decline will be highlighted. The motivation for collecting multimodal data that includes MRI, OCT, Gait, etc. will be presented. The use of proteomics and genomics coupled with digital data presents a huge opportunity to develop sophisticated data analysis tools to build a composite biomarker for early detection of the onset of the disease. These predictive tools would enable designing appropriate intervention mechanisms to halt or delay the progress of the disease.

Bio: K V S Hari is a Professor in the Department of ECE, Indian Institute of Science, Bangalore. He holds a BE (ECE) degree from Osmania University, Hyderabad, MTech (Radar and Communication Systems) from IIT Delhi and PhD (Systems Science) from U C San Diego and has been a visiting faculty at Stanford University and Affiliate Professor at KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Stockholm. His research interests include 5G wireless communications, radar systems, autonomous vehicles, neuroscience, and affordable MRI systems. He is a co-author of the IEEE 802.16 standard on wireless channel models. He is a Fellow of the Indian National Academy of Engineering and a Fellow of IEEE. He is currently the Director, Centre for Brain Research at IISc.
More details at http://ece.iisc.ac.in/~hari


ALL ARE WELCOME.

Thank you,
CNI Seminar Series Organizing Committee.
